official.deadline_note: MOE publishes no single deadline for this index - each award sets its own window. Published windows as at 10 October 2026: MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term) - GCE A-Level applicants apply from the release of results to 19 March 2027, the Polytechnic Diploma window opens early February 2027, NUS High School early December 2026, and IB and international qualifications mid-October 2026, with the intervening periods currently closed; the PSC Scholarship (Teaching Service) applications for 2027 are open and close 15 March 2027; MOE Pre-University Scholarship - 12 October 2026 to 11 November 2026 (11.59pm) for Integrated Programme students, with all other students applying from January 2027; ASEAN Scholarship - applications for all countries are now closed (the 2026 country windows ran from 5 January to 23 February or 23 March 2026).
official.application_cycle: 2027 cycle for the undergraduate and pre-university awards (MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award and PSC Teaching Service closing 15-19 March 2027, other teaching windows opening from mid-October 2026; MOE Pre-University Scholarship Integrated Programme window 12 October - 11 November 2026, other students from January 2027); the ASEAN Scholarship 2026 round is closed for every country with a 2027 mailing list open.
official.status_note: MOE's awards and scholarships index is live (page last updated 12 March 2026) and lists the awards currently on offer. Within it: the MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term) application page (last updated 14 September 2026) states that PSC Scholarships for 2027 are now open and close 15 March 2027 and that the GCE A-Level window runs to 19 March 2027; the MOE-AU Scholarship page states Full-term and Mid-term applications are open on PSC Gateway; the ASEAN Scholarship hub states applications for all countries are now closed.
official.tuition_coverage_note: MOE publishes coverage per award rather than for the index: the MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award offers 'full coverage of your undergraduate tuition fees' and 'tuition fees and other approved charges'; the MOE-AU Scholarship covers 'all tuition and compulsory fees'; the ASEAN Scholarship covers school fees and GCE O-Level and A-Level examination fees; the MOE Pre-University Scholarship covers school fees at Singapore Citizen rates less subsidies, subject to an annual cap of $2,400, alongside an annual allowance of $750. Edusave, ESIS and UPLIFT are cash awards rather than fee subsidies.
benefits: MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term): full coverage of undergraduate tuition fees, a monthly maintenance allowance, return economy airfare when studying overseas, developmental programmes, approved student exchange, summer programmes and CCAs, and possible sponsorship of a Master's degree if requirements are met

MOE-AU Scholarship: all tuition and compulsory fees, acceptance fees paid to the institution of study, maintenance and other allowances, visa and immigration-related fees where applicable, economy airfare for scholars studying overseas, sponsorship of approved overseas field trips, immersion programmes or summer school courses, and one overseas exchange for scholars studying locally
MOE Pre-University Scholarship: an annual allowance of $750 plus school fees based on Singapore Citizen rates less subsidies, subject to an annual cap of $2,400

ASEAN Scholarship: annual allowance with hostel accommodation, settling-in allowance, return economy airfare (or return transport allowance for West Malaysians), school fees, examination fees for GCE O-Level and A-Level once as applicable, and subsidised medical benefits and accident insurance cover

Edusave scholarships for Independent Schools (ESIS): scholarships of up to $2,400 per year; UPLIFT Scholarship: cash awards of $1,200 per year; the Centennial Fund Award, ITE Progression Award, special awards and programme-specific scholarships are also listed on the index
eligibility: Edusave awards and scholarships are offered to Singapore Citizen students based on their character, leadership, conduct, learning dispositions and academic performance

MOE Pre-University Scholarship: Singapore Citizens, or non-Citizens with at least 1 parent who is a Singapore Citizen, with a GCE O-Level aggregate score of 8 points or less (without bonus points) in English and Higher Mother Tongue or Mother Tongue and 5 relevant subjects, plus a good co-curricular activities record and a good conduct record; recipients must not hold another MOE scholarship concurrently except the Edusave Scholarships for Independent Schools

MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term): Singapore Citizen at point of offer, a well-rounded individual with good academic and co-curricular activities records, GCE A-Level, International Baccalaureate Diploma, Polytechnic Diploma, NUS High School Diploma or equivalent, strong leadership qualities and excellent interpersonal and communication skills

MOE-AU Scholarship: Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents who take up Singapore Citizenship before the award, with a strong interest in an academic career at NUS, NTU, SMU, SUTD, SIT or SUSS; the full-term award is for those who have completed pre-university examinations or hold the qualifications, the mid-term award for undergraduates past their first semester who are not in their final year

ASEAN Scholarship: nationals of participating ASEAN countries (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam) who are proficient in English, have done consistently well in school examinations and have a good record of participation in co-curricular activities
requirements: MOE Pre-University Scholarship: a valid SingPass account with 2-Factor Authentication to reach the application system at go.gov.sg/moescholarshipsystem, registration as a new user with a valid personal email, and completion of all sections before the 11.59pm close
MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term): an online application form complete with the necessary supporting documents, submitted during the window for the applicant's qualification type
MOE-AU Scholarship: an application on PSC Gateway in which 'Academia' is indicated as one of the career choices
ASEAN Scholarship: an online application during the country's own window, then attendance at selection tests and a selection interview if shortlisted
selection_criteria: Edusave awards and scholarships are granted on character, leadership, conduct, learning dispositions and academic performance

MOE Pre-University Scholarship: outstanding academic results and excellence in co-curricular and other activities; Integrated Programme students are nominated by their school for interviews commencing in February, other students are invited on their GCE O-Level results with interviews from late April to May, and successful candidates are notified in August

MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term): academic and co-curricular record, leadership, and interpersonal and communication skills; shortlisted applicants are scheduled for interviews and other selection processes and can generally expect to hear within 4 weeks of the close of the window

ASEAN Scholarship: consistent performance in school examinations plus a co-curricular record, then selection tests and interviews held in the applicant's own country (for example Bandung, Jakarta and Surabaya in Indonesia, or Johor Bahru, Kuala Lumpur, Kuching and Penang in Malaysia)
MOE-AU Scholarship: high achievement and aptitude for the academic field or subject the applicant wishes to specialise in, with a strong interest in an academic career
coverage: MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term): tuition fees and other approved charges, monthly maintenance and pre-service allowance, return economy airfare if studying overseas, developmental programmes during undergraduate studies, approved exchange and summer programmes and CCAs, with a bond of 4 years for local studies, 5 years for studies in non-English speaking countries and 6 years for studies in English speaking countries, plus a concurrent 3-year bond if the PGDE is taken at NIE

MOE-AU Scholarship: full sponsorship for undergraduate courses of any field and at any reputable local or overseas university subject to the Scholarship Board's approval, covering all tuition and compulsory fees, acceptance fees, maintenance and other allowances, visa and immigration fees, economy airfare for overseas study, approved overseas field trips, immersion programmes or summer school, and one overseas exchange for scholars at a local institution, followed by a PhD scholarship under START and a 4 to 6 year bond as academic staff in the paired autonomous university

ASEAN Scholarship: annual allowance with hostel accommodation, settling-in allowance, return economy airfare, school fees, examination fees for GCE O-Level and A-Level (once only, as applicable) and subsidised medical benefits and accident insurance cover; each scholarship leads to the Singapore-Cambridge GCE A-Level certificate or similar qualification and is renewed annually on school performance
MOE Pre-University Scholarship: annual allowance of $750 and school fees based on Singapore Citizen rates less any subsidies, subject to an annual cap of $2,400, awarded for 2 years

Published cash values on the MOE index: Edusave scholarships for Independent Schools up to $2,400 per year, UPLIFT Scholarship cash awards of $1,200 per year, and the MOE Pre-University Scholarship at up to $2,400 per year
application_method: MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (Full-Term): apply directly to MOE through the online application form inside the window for your qualification, or apply for the PSC-administered Scholarship (Teaching Service) through the PSC Gateway

MOE Pre-University Scholarship: register at go.gov.sg/moescholarshipsystem with your SingPass, complete every section of the form, submit, and keep the acknowledgement email with the application reference number
MOE-AU Scholarship: apply on the PSC Gateway indicating 'Academia' as one of the career choices; enquiries go to MOE_AU_Scholarship@moe.gov.sg
ASEAN Scholarship: submit the online application during the country window and, if shortlisted, attend the selection tests and interview in your own country
official.application_route: Start from the MOE awards and scholarships index and then use the route of the specific award: the MOE scholarship system with SingPass for the Pre-University Scholarship, the MOE online form or PSC Gateway for the teaching awards, PSC Gateway for the MOE-AU Scholarship, and the country-specific online form for the ASEAN Scholarship.
official.citizenship_residency: Edusave awards, the MOE Pre-University Scholarship, ESIS, UPLIFT and the MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award are framed around Singapore Citizen students (the Pre-University Scholarship also admits non-Citizens with at least one Singapore Citizen parent); the MOE-AU Scholarship is for Citizens or Permanent Residents who take up citizenship before the award; the ASEAN Scholarship is for nationals of participating ASEAN countries.
official.international_eligibility: Only through the ASEAN Scholarship, which is the award on MOE's page intended for nationals of Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam; every other award listed is framed around Singapore Citizen students.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The MOE-AU Scholarship is open to undergraduate courses of any field at a local autonomous university and tracks scholars towards an academic career; the MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award expects a course relevant to a teaching subject (Art and Music, Humanities, Languages, Mathematics, Physical Education and Sports Science, Sciences, Social Sciences) while applicants for other similar courses are still accepted and advised later on assigned teaching subjects; the ASEAN Scholarship is for secondary or pre-university study in selected Singapore secondary schools and junior colleges.
official.duration: MOE Pre-University Scholarship: 2 years. ASEAN Scholarship: 6 years from Secondary 1, 4 years from Secondary 3 and 2 years from Pre-university 1, renewed each year on school performance. MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award: the length of the undergraduate degree with a service bond of 4 years for local study, 5 years for a non-English speaking country and 6 years for an English speaking country, plus a concurrent 3-year PGDE bond. MOE-AU Scholarship: undergraduate study, then a PhD scholarship under START, then a 4 to 6 year bond as academic staff.
official.description: Singapore's Ministry of Education administers the country's main education awards: school and pre-university awards for Singapore Citizen students, the ASEAN Scholarship for students from ASEAN countries, and undergraduate scholarships (the MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award and the MOE-AU Scholarship) that fund study in return for service. MOE presents them through one awards and scholarships index, with each award publishing its own value, eligibility and deadline.
official.program_type: Ministry/index-level entry spanning school, pre-university and undergraduate awards administered by MOE and the Public Service Commission
official.english_requirement: The ASEAN Scholarship requires applicants to be proficient in English, as stated on the country pages (for example the Malaysia and Indonesia pages). MOE publishes no English test or medium-of-instruction requirement for the other awards listed on the index.

applicant_utility.summary: This row covers MOE's whole award family, so decide first which door is yours: Singapore Citizens and PRs heading for university should look at the MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award (A-Level window closes 19 March 2027, other qualification windows open from mid-October 2026 to February 2027) or the MOE-AU Scholarship through PSC Gateway, while Integrated Programme students have a narrow 12 October to 11 November 2026 window for the Pre-University Scholarship. Non-Singaporeans realistically have only the ASEAN Scholarship, and its 2026 round is closed in every country, so the smart move now is joining the MOE mailing list and preparing for the country windows that open between January and April 2027. In every case the real number and the real deadline sit on the individual award's page, not on the index.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Singaporean undergraduates who want a teaching or academic career funded end to end, Singaporean pre-university students chasing the $2,400-capped Pre-University Scholarship, and ASEAN nationals in secondary school targeting the ASEAN Scholarship.
application_readiness_checklist: Establish which of the four routes is yours - Pre-University Scholarship, MOE Teaching Scholarships/Award, MOE-AU Scholarship or ASEAN Scholarship - since each has its own portal, window and eligibility base

Integrated Programme students: register at go.gov.sg/moescholarshipsystem early and get SingPass with 2FA working before the 11 November 2026 close, because MOE itself warns that SingPass and Myinfo setup takes time
A-Level applicants: apply as soon as results are released, since the window shuts on 19 March 2027 and MOE schedules interviews in the order applications arrive
For the MOE-AU Scholarship, build the PSC Gateway application around a concrete academic career and remember to list 'Academia' as one of the career choices
ASEAN applicants: join MOE's mailing list now and track your own country's window, which historically opens between January and April rather than on a single national date
common_rejection_risks: Missing a qualification-specific teaching window: the A-Level route runs from results release to 19 March 2027, while IB and international qualifications (mid-October 2026), NUS High School (early December 2026) and Polytechnic (early February 2027) open at different times and are closed in between
Applying to the ASEAN Scholarship outside your country's window - the 2026 round is closed everywhere and each country runs its own dates
Already holding another MOE scholarship: Pre-University Scholarship recipients may not hold a concurrent MOE scholarship other than ESIS
Underestimating the service bond - 4 to 6 years of teaching service for the undergraduate teaching awards, plus a concurrent 3-year bond for trainees on the PGDE at NIE
Reading the Pre-University Scholarship's $2,400 as an allowance: it is a cap on school fees, with only $750 a year paid as allowance
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: For school-level awards the published figures are allowances and fee subsidies rather than full cost coverage, so families still carry school fees above the $2,400 annual cap plus living, transport and enrichment costs. For the undergraduate teaching and MOE-AU awards MOE publishes no allowance figure, so personal spending beyond tuition, maintenance allowance and approved airfare must be self-funded, and the ASEAN Scholarship leaves costs beyond school fees, exam fees, accommodation and medical cover to the scholar.
document_audit: No MOE page publishes a document checklist - the teaching awards ask for an online form 'complete with the necessary supporting documents' without naming them, so prepare qualification certificates and CCA records proactively

The Pre-University Scholarship application pulls particulars through SingPass Myinfo, so your registered particulars and email address must be current before submission or the pre-filled data will be wrong
ASEAN applicants are tested and interviewed in their own country and only shortlisted candidates are notified, so keep email and phone contact active over the whole window
Teaching-award interviews arrive at most four weeks after the window closes, so have certificates, CCA evidence and oral talking points ready in advance rather than after shortlisting
alerts: The A-Level teaching window closes 19 March 2027 and the PSC Scholarship (Teaching Service) route closes 15 March 2027, with shortlisted candidates informed at least a week before tests and interviews
ASEAN Scholarship applications are closed for all countries as at 10 October 2026; the 2027 windows reopen by country, with mailing-list subscribers notified first

The teaching awards bind you to 4 to 6 years of service (plus a concurrent 3-year PGDE bond at NIE) and the MOE-AU Scholarship binds you to 4 to 6 years as academic staff after your PhD - this is a career commitment, not just funding
Only the ASEAN Scholarship on this page is open to non-Singaporeans; every other listed award is framed around Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents willing to take up citizenship
Mailing lists (go.gov.sg/moecareersml for MOE scholarships, the form.gov.sg ASEAN list) are the only advance notice MOE gives of windows reopening
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online inside your route's window - MOE scholarship system, the MOE careers application form, or PSC Gateway - then wait for shortlisting, sit tests and interviews, and receive offers by email, with the school routes running through MOE systems and the undergraduate routes through MOE or the Public Service Commission.
